channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Hydrophobic Fountain" - An old, sentient fountain doesn't want people to climb on it.

item.title: Re: Hydrophobic Fountain
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

While I like the core idea of a sentient fountain that produces hydrophia, I have a few concerns regarding it. The first one, and the most important, is about the way you're going to portray the fountain's consciousness. How are you going to do it? How does it communicate? Does it have a personality? Why did it decide to induce hydrophobia to the whole town?

My second concern is about the way you're going to structure the article. Are you going to do interviews, reports, journals, some kind of radio transmissions…? Are you planning to show the affected people's point of view?

This draft is about 2-3 years old.

While I think that the site's expectations have evolved, I've seen articles that old being still good ones, so I'm unsure whether this will affect the result or not.

Overall, and with the awareness that 'many reviewers liked it', I'm going to ask you to PM me a link to your draft. I would like to see how you developed this concept to make sure this is still up to the site expectations.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlights) Hydrophobic Fountain
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A sentient fountain that doesn't want to be played in or climbed on creates hydrophobia-inducing water.

Central Narrative: School-kids on their senior year start spreading a local legend among their younger peers and other people to not to interact with a certain fountain. One day, a pipe of the fountain is burst by the fountain, spreading a town’s water supply, creating a hydrophobic town.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fountain itself and its experience as a structure that's always been alive for years.

Additional Notes: This is an old idea that already has a draft, as it was liked by many reviewers back when it was first made, both in IRC chatrooms and forum posts. (This draft is about 2-3 years old.) I took a long hiatus from skip writing, but I may be returning to finish this skip. I wonder if the idea itself has aged well, but I might as well see if it gets greenlit so I can advance it towards the draft forum and hope to get it published soon. Despite trying to write skips 2-3 years ago, am I still considered a first-time author?
